# Trump’s Battle with the Fed Explained | The Real Eisman Playbook Episode 25

First listed: 2025-09-15 | Evaluation cutoff: 2026-11-10

[Back to library](../README.md)

## Source versions

- [YouTube: Trump’s Battle with the Fed Explained | The Real Eisman Playbook Episode 25](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cdXMf6KoMpc) - 2025-09-15
- [Substack: Trump’s Battle with the Fed Explained | The Real Eisman Playbook Episode 25](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/trumps-battle-with-the-fed-explained-0b1) - 2025-09-15

Earliest listed publication among matched versions, not proof of an unedited contemporaneous archive. Claim timestamps refer to the reviewed version.

## Summary

Former Dallas Fed president Robert Kaplan explains the tension between weak hiring and inflation, the case for a quarter-point September rate cut, and how policymakers use business contacts. The conversation moves to tariffs, factory investment, merger integration, Goldman’s client strategy and bank consolidation. Eisman explicitly agrees with the 25-basis-point call and advances a technology-scale argument for bank mergers.

The September 2025 rate-cut forecast is a clear bounded success for Kaplan and for Eisman’s explicit endorsement. Most claims about private Fed deliberations, business sentiment and the causes of inflation remain insufficiently identified for a binary outcome grade. Kaplan’s claim that Goldman eliminated client conflicts is contradicted by the firm’s own risk disclosures. His management views and merger recommendations remain separate from Eisman’s forecasts.

## Material claims

<a id="youtube-cdXMf6KoMpc-c001"></a>
### 001. The US president appointed Kaplan to lead the Dallas Fed.

**Wrong** | Steve Eisman | material factual premise | supporting

[Source at 1:49-1:54](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cdXMf6KoMpc&t=109s) | Stance: corrected_in_dialogue | Horizon: not stated

Kaplan immediately corrects the tentative introduction, and Eisman accepts the correction. Reserve Bank presidents are selected by eligible directors with Board approval.

Qualification: Eisman says he guesses this was an Obama appointment; the guest immediately explains otherwise.

Assessment test: Check the Reserve Bank appointment process, distinct from the Board of Governors.

- [Selection of Reserve Bank presidents](https://www.federalreserve.gov/faqs/how-is-a-federal-reserve-bank-president-selected.htm) (inspected 2026-11-10): Class B and C Reserve Bank directors appoint the president, subject to Board of Governors approval. It is not a presidential appointment.

<a id="youtube-cdXMf6KoMpc-c002"></a>
### 002. A regional Fed president is selected by the local board and approved by the Board of Governors.

**Right** | Robert Kaplan | material factual premise | supporting

[Source at 1:54-2:06](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cdXMf6KoMpc&t=114s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The official process supports Kaplan’s correction; only Class B and C directors participate in this appointment.

Assessment test: Distinguish eligible directors from bank-affiliated Class A directors.

- [Selection of Reserve Bank presidents](https://www.federalreserve.gov/faqs/how-is-a-federal-reserve-bank-president-selected.htm) (inspected 2026-11-10): Class B and C Reserve Bank directors appoint the president, subject to Board of Governors approval. It is not a presidential appointment.

<a id="youtube-cdXMf6KoMpc-c012"></a>
### 012. A real neutral rate around 0.75% implies nominal neutral near 3.5%, leaving only 75-100 basis points of easing room.

**Unresolved** | Robert Kaplan | explanation | major

[Source at 5:34-6:10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cdXMf6KoMpc&t=334s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The addition is arithmetically valid under the chosen inflation assumption, but neutral is an uncertain estimated equilibrium, not an observed policy target. Current inflation need not equal expected equilibrium inflation.

Assessment test: Identify expected inflation and the neutral-rate model; test a range rather than a point estimate.

<a id="youtube-cdXMf6KoMpc-c031"></a>
### 031. If neutral rises while the policy rate remains fixed at zero, policy becomes more accommodative relative to neutral.

**Right** | Robert Kaplan | explanation | major

[Source at 20:42-21:08](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cdXMf6KoMpc&t=1242s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

This is a conditional policy-gap relationship. It does not prove how much neutral actually rose or quantify the subsequent inflation effect.

Conditional reasoning: Policy gap = actual real rate - neutral real rate. Holding the actual rate fixed while neutral rises makes the gap more negative.

Assessment test: Estimate neutral separately and compare the real policy-rate gap.

<a id="youtube-cdXMf6KoMpc-c044"></a>
### 044. Goldman has eliminated client conflicts because capital commitments are always on behalf of clients.

**Wrong** | Robert Kaplan | explanation | major

[Source at 33:41-33:45](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cdXMf6KoMpc&t=2021s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

Goldman’s own annual filing describes ongoing potential conflicts involving client services and its investments, and warns that cross-division collaboration can increase them. Managing conflicts is different from eliminating them.

Assessment test: Compare the absolute assertion with risk disclosures and actual transaction structures.

- [2024 Form 10-K, conflicts and business changes](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/886982/000088698225000005/gs-20241231.htm) (2025): Goldman discloses continuing actual or potential client conflicts, including its own investments; One Goldman Sachs may increase conflicts. It also reports narrowed consumer activities and remaining principal investments.

<a id="youtube-cdXMf6KoMpc-c045"></a>
### 045. Committing capital for clients deserves a higher earnings multiple than proprietary risk-taking.

**Unresolved** | Robert Kaplan | explanation | major

[Source at 33:48-33:51](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cdXMf6KoMpc&t=2028s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

This is a relative valuation hypothesis. Fee stability, risk, capital use and price must be specified before a causal premium can be measured.

Assessment test: Compare business mix, required capital, earnings volatility and valuation on a consistent basis.


<a id="youtube-cdXMf6KoMpc-c046"></a>
### 046. One Goldman Sachs substantially improves cross-division collaboration and client service.

**Unresolved** | Robert Kaplan | explanation | major

[Source at 33:54-34:35](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cdXMf6KoMpc&t=2034s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The initiative exists, but Kaplan’s appraisal is an interested management assessment rather than independent evidence of incremental client outcomes.

Assessment test: Measure cross-selling, retention, client satisfaction and conflicts alongside financial results.


<a id="youtube-cdXMf6KoMpc-c047"></a>
### 047. As an organization grows, engagement and leadership development become harder and more valuable.

**Not testable** | Robert Kaplan | analytical principle | major

[Source at 34:38-36:27](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cdXMf6KoMpc&t=2078s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

This is a management judgment and account of Kaplan’s work. It is not a quantified relationship between staffing and returns.

Assessment test: Treat as a stated preference or framework; define an observable test before grading an outcome.


<a id="youtube-cdXMf6KoMpc-c048"></a>
### 048. A past Goldman culture treated clients like counterparties, and Solomon implicitly acknowledged a need to restore client focus.

Eisman reports a journalist’s argument and his interpretation of a private conversation. A nod is not an independently verified admission or proof of every historical allegation.

Assessment test: Consult original reporting and attributable public or documentary evidence.


<a id="youtube-cdXMf6KoMpc-c049"></a>
### 049. Putting clients and employees first is the central principle Kaplan believes Goldman has restored.

**Not testable** | Robert Kaplan | analytical principle | major

[Source at 38:59-40:26](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cdXMf6KoMpc&t=2339s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

This is a stated aspiration and personal assessment; it does not cancel the firm’s disclosed conflicts or independently verify cultural change.

Assessment test: Treat as a stated preference or framework; define an observable test before grading an outcome.


<a id="youtube-cdXMf6KoMpc-c050"></a>
### 050. Morgan Stanley expanded wealth management through E*TRADE and other acquisitions as part of Gorman’s business transformation.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 40:31-40:52](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cdXMf6KoMpc&t=2431s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The issuer confirms completion and the enlarged wealth-management franchise. Eisman’s qualitative praise of the strategy is distinct from a fully measured return or capital-intensity comparison.

Assessment test: Compare transaction completion and subsequent segment mix before evaluating value creation.

- [Morgan Stanley closes E*TRADE acquisition](https://www.morganstanley.com/press-releases/morgan-stanley-closes-acquisition-of-e-trade) (2020-10-02): The completed acquisition expanded the wealth-management franchise. Closing does not independently prove every projected financial benefit.

<a id="youtube-cdXMf6KoMpc-c051"></a>

**Right** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

The annual filing documents exits and losses across consumer-related activities, supporting the description of retrenchment.

Assessment test: Check the disposed businesses, remaining obligations and realized costs.

- [2024 Form 10-K, conflicts and business changes](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/886982/000088698225000005/gs-20241231.htm) (2025): Goldman discloses continuing actual or potential client conflicts, including its own investments; One Goldman Sachs may increase conflicts. It also reports narrowed consumer activities and remaining principal investments.

<a id="youtube-cdXMf6KoMpc-c052"></a>
### 052. Goldman’s T. Rowe Price collaboration should improve its retirement and wealth franchise.

**Too early** | Robert Kaplan | forecast | major

[Source at 41:19-42:15](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cdXMf6KoMpc&t=2479s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: future franchise development

The collaboration was announced, but the guest provides no measurable return target or completion date for the expected franchise benefits.

Assessment test: Track launched products, client flows, fees and risk rather than score the announcement itself as success.

- [Goldman Sachs and T. Rowe Price strategic collaboration](https://www.goldmansachs.com/pressroom/press-releases/2025/announcement-04-september-2025) (2025-09-04): The firms announced collaboration on public-private investment products for retirement and wealth investors; benefits remain prospective.

<a id="youtube-cdXMf6KoMpc-c053"></a>
### 053. Post-crisis capital requirements and stress tests materially changed how large financial firms manage their balance sheets.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 42:18-43:17](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cdXMf6KoMpc&t=2538s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The supervisory stress-test framework verifies this institutional change. Passing a specified scenario is not proof of immunity to every failure.

Assessment test: Review capital rules, scenario assumptions and actual supervisory coverage.

- [2025 stress-test results, revised September 30](https://www.federalreserve.gov/publications/2025-june-dodd-frank-act-stress-test-results.htm) (2025-06-27): Aggregate CET1 13.4% at start, hypothetical trough 11.6%; institution-specific outcomes and separate leverage ratios are disclosed. Results reflect scenario, portfolio and model assumptions, not a direct measure of political intent.

<a id="youtube-cdXMf6KoMpc-c054"></a>
### 054. Nonbank finance is concerning because it lacks the same bank stress-testing regime.

**Unresolved** | Robert Kaplan | explanation | major

[Source at 42:41-43:17](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cdXMf6KoMpc&t=2561s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The perimeter difference is a useful concern, but nonbanks are heterogeneous and the comment does not establish a specific failure or absence of every form of oversight.

Assessment test: Map entity-specific regulation, stress tests, liquidity promises and risk concentration.


<a id="youtube-cdXMf6KoMpc-c055"></a>
### 055. SVB exposed glaring interest-rate and liquidity mismatches that supervisors failed to address promptly.

**Right** | Robert Kaplan | explanation | major

[Source at 43:23-44:20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cdXMf6KoMpc&t=2603s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The Fed’s review supports management failure and inadequate supervisory escalation. Kaplan’s stronger claim that excessive regulatory breadth was the decisive cause is not established.

Assessment test: Separate documented risk-management failures from competing explanations for supervisory delay.

- [SVB review key takeaways](https://www.federalreserve.gov/publications/2023-April-SVB-Key-Takeaways.htm) (2023-05-17): Management failed to manage interest and liquidity risks; supervisors identified deficiencies but acted too slowly. Tailoring reduced standards, but stronger rules may not have prevented failure.

<a id="youtube-cdXMf6KoMpc-c056"></a>

The review documents supervisory failures, but that does not isolate regulatory overload as the causal mechanism.

Assessment test: Compare supervisory priorities, staffing, escalation and the effect of tailoring using contemporaneous records.


<a id="youtube-cdXMf6KoMpc-c057"></a>

This is a policy prescription. Its effect on failures, credit availability and competition requires a specific reform and counterfactual.

Assessment test: Treat as a stated preference or framework; define an observable test before grading an outcome.

The categorical characterization needs a dated application and approval series; the episode supplies no such comparison.

<a id="youtube-cdXMf6KoMpc-c059"></a>
### 059. Large banks enjoy a major technology and deposit-gathering advantage because smaller rivals cannot afford comparable investment.

**Unresolved** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 45:27-45:46](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cdXMf6KoMpc&t=2727s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The scale mechanism is plausible, but the magnitude and universality of the disadvantage are not established. Vendor platforms and specialized franchises can change the comparison.

Assessment test: Compare technology spend, unit costs, deposit growth and customer behavior by bank size.


<a id="youtube-cdXMf6KoMpc-c060"></a>
### 060. The $250,000 deposit-insurance limit gives the biggest banks an advantage in attracting large deposits.

**Unresolved** | Robert Kaplan | explanation | major

[Source at 45:48-45:55](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cdXMf6KoMpc&t=2748s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

Perceived safety can affect flows, but insurance varies by ownership category and bank, and the causal size advantage needs evidence. The same nominal rule applies across insured banks.

Assessment test: Compare uninsured-deposit flows, account categories and perceived government support.


<a id="youtube-cdXMf6KoMpc-c061"></a>

**Not testable** | Steve Eisman | analytical principle | major

This is Eisman’s strategic prescription, not a dated forecast that a particular merger wave will occur. Larger size alone does not guarantee better competition.

Assessment test: Treat as a stated preference or framework; define an observable test before grading an outcome.


<a id="youtube-cdXMf6KoMpc-c062"></a>
### 062. The US has about 4,150 banks and only about 80 with assets above $20 billion.

**Unresolved** | Robert Kaplan | explanation | supporting

[Source at 46:14-46:23](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cdXMf6KoMpc&t=2774s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The exact counts depend on date and whether banks, thrifts, charters or holding companies are counted. A matched distribution was not inspected.

Assessment test: Reconcile both counts to the same regulatory population and reporting date.


<a id="youtube-cdXMf6KoMpc-c063"></a>
### 063. Substantial consolidation among smaller and mid-sized banks is likely and should improve competitive capacity.

**Too early** | Robert Kaplan | forecast | major

[Source at 46:24-46:48](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cdXMf6KoMpc&t=2784s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: future consolidation, no exact endpoint

There is no stated deadline or quantitative merger threshold. The competition benefit also depends on geography, pricing and integration rather than size alone.

Assessment test: Define a prospective horizon and track mergers, market concentration and customer outcomes.


<a id="youtube-cdXMf6KoMpc-c064"></a>
### 064. Federal debt/GDP rose from the mid-70s before COVID to over 100%.

**Unresolved** | Robert Kaplan | explanation | supporting

[Source at 46:50-46:58](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cdXMf6KoMpc&t=2810s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The comparison does not specify gross debt versus debt held by the public or a precise baseline and endpoint. Switching definitions would invalidate the inference.

Assessment test: Use one debt definition and consistent fiscal or calendar-year GDP throughout.


<a id="youtube-cdXMf6KoMpc-c065"></a>
### 065. Bank consolidation and better regulation can free capital, increase private growth and help reduce debt relative to GDP.

**Unresolved** | Robert Kaplan | conditional scenario | major

[Source at 46:58-47:35](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cdXMf6KoMpc&t=2818s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The multi-step causal chain is conditional. More lending need not improve productivity, and a debt ratio also depends on deficits, interest costs and nominal GDP.

Assessment test: Estimate capital release, loan quality, incremental output and the fiscal path separately.


## Framework and tools

- Ask how a policy affects labor supply, prices, investment timing and business margins separately.
- Use business contacts as a complement to economic releases while recognizing selection and revision risk.
- Separate a completed merger agreement from the integration that creates or destroys value.
- Compare fee-oriented client businesses with principal risk and check whether conflicts are managed rather than assumed absent.
- Treat bank technology scale and consolidation as hypotheses requiring franchise and competition evidence.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- Dual mandate, labor-force supply, inflation measures and the estimated neutral policy rate.
- FOMC voting structure and the role of regional business outreach.
- Tariff-sensitive import margins, housing affordability and factory expensing.
- Merger integration, client franchises, capital requirements and stress testing.
- Bank size distribution, deposit competition and public-debt/GDP definitions.

## Source cautions

Steve Eisman interviews Robert Kaplan. Kaplan owns his policy, management and Goldman assessments; Eisman’s explicit comments and adoptions are separately recorded.
- Read every caption segment through the closing disclosure.
- Opening preview repeats later passages and is not counted as extra claims.
- Kaplan supplies most substantive answers; Eisman’s questions do not automatically endorse them. His 25-basis-point prediction is an explicit exception.
- The source refers to the September 2025 FOMC decision prospectively. Goldman/T. Rowe Price collaboration was announced September 4; an exact recording date is not asserted.
- Captions confuse names and contain an inconsistent return-to-Goldman year. Incidental career chronology is not used as an investment forecast.
